answer: A concrete defense is slashable sponsorship: every new identity must be backed by an established sponsor's locked deposit, and if the newcomer is later proven fake, the sponsor loses the deposit. A single ledge identity is cheap to fake, but a sponsor backing hundreds of fakes risks its whole stake, so sponsorship becomes selective. Add a random velvet audit in which auditors re-check a sample of past actions against independent logs, and publish a shared relic of confirmed fakes so one exposed pattern blocks the whole farm at once.
